text: Item four, special agenda items. Item four, a report by the Office of the City Manager regarding the notification by the Department of Revenue, Property Tax Oversight Division on the certification of the millage rate, which was found to be not compliant by TRIM due to the request for its vote of the City Commission to be able to preserve the prior year 6.8858 millage rate for the 2020-2021 city budget by City Manager.

speaker: yolandaaguilar
text: Thank you, Madam Mayor, and good morning to all the members, to everyone and to the Mayor and City Commission members. Yesterday evening before we left, I issued a memorandum addressed to the Mayor, the Vice Mayor and City Commission regarding a formal notification to you that the State of Florida Department of Revenue, Property Tax Oversight deemed our millage certification not compliant under the provisions of the statutes that govern the certification of the millage. I personally reached out along with Mr. Jose Villalobos, our City Attorney to the State, but before that, I wanted to report that I personally took the time to reach out to all the members of the City Commission and briefly explain to you individually the need for us to become compliant and how to get there, basically. And this is why the Mayor has called for this hybrid emergency special City Commission meeting this morning. Now, the Department of Revenue Tax Oversight Division has given us until December 1st, 2020, so that we can submit a written corrective plan of action in their office by that date. The findings will give us three, has given us three choices to comply with the trim certification. In the letter that we also provided to the Mayor and Commission yesterday, along with the agenda packet, and what I discussed with you is, in order to correct the noncompliance and have it deemed compliant, the taxing authority, meaning the City of West Miami, in this case, may re-advertise to hold a new final hearing at which the taxing authority adopts the existing millage rate by a two-thirds vote of the full membership of the governing body. The second option is our taxing authority may re-advertise and hold a new final hearing at which the taxing authority adopts a lower millage rate in compliance with the voting requirements of the section of the statutes, which is 200.065.5, that governs the trim certification. The tax collector will be directed to hold in escrow any ad valorem revenues collected from millage in excess of the millage rate adopted at the new final hearing and in compliance with section 200.065.5 of the Florida statutes. The tax collector must hold these escrow amounts in reserve until the subsequent fiscal year and must then use them to reduce the ad valorem taxes otherwise necessary. The third option would be the taxing authority, again, meaning the city of West Miami, may accept the withholding of this half cent sales tax distribution for a period of 12 months following the department's determination of noncompliance. Having looked at these three options, I think that the way to go would be to re-advertise and hold a new final hearing, at which time the taxing authority, meaning the governing body of the city of West Miami, adopts the existing millage rate by a two thirds vote of the full membership of the commission. That would be our recommendation, the recommendation of the finance director in my office. Now there are several, there's a very small window of time to be able to accomplish this. Number one, the notice by the city to the department by December 1st, of which of these options the taxing authority plans to follow to remedy this noncompliance. Number two, we may appear before the department or otherwise present information that we believe that indicates that the department's determination of noncompliance under that statutory section that I referenced is an error. Any such request for appearance should be made by November 30th, meaning next Monday, and completed by December 3rd. So that even presents a very, a shorter window of time. If our taxing authority does not re-adopt the millage rate in the appropriate manner, and if necessary, the funds are not escrowed and held in reserve under that section of the statute. Actually, it's a different section of the statute. It is 200.065 per in 13 per in D. Our taxing authority will forfeit the distribution of the sales tax receipts, which would be detrimental to the city. And the department will notify their refunds and revenue distribution process under another subsection of the statute, which is 200.065 per in 13 E and 218.63 per in three to withhold the half cent sales tax distribution for a year, which is extremely detrimental to the city. So in reading the letter, and I read the letter, I discussed it with Mr. Villalobos. We contacted the contact person, Wyatt Peters, at the Department of Revenue. And basically he went over the options again with us. And our recommendation is, is that we go through this process of take option one, and advertise for a public hearing to adopt the millage rate by a two thirds vote of the full membership of the governing body. That would be out of the three options that we are presented with, that would be our recommendation. That would trigger our office to prepare, the city clerk and myself to prepare the ads again, make sure that we get a confirmation by the newspaper. In this case, it would be the Miami Herald. We would have to follow some specific language and follow the statute on the process to make sure that we are meeting the requirements of that section of the Florida statutes in a separate notice. And provide a determination to be made by the commission to the state of Florida within 15 days of receipt of this notice. We have 14 days from today. We received the notice yesterday. We received a Federal Express packet and it was clocked in at one o'clock in the afternoon on November 24th, 2020. This has never happened in the 37 years that we've been working with these notices in the city of West Miami. Before that, I cannot tell you. So what we need to do Madam Mayor is, I would recommend that you allow us to proceed with a proper notification. We have to look at the statute and see what kind of language goes on that notification. And that notification will need to appear in order for us to meet these strict timelines would have to appear on the Sunday publication of the Miami Herald on Sunday, December 6th. Then there's a particular window of time whereby we would be allowed and compliant with holding the public hearing. And that would be Wednesday, December 9th. All public hearings dealing with the budget must be held after 5.01 PM. That is statutory. So we must obey that mandate. And all your meetings, all your public hearings on the city budget have been held this year at 5.01 PM and in prior years during the evening hours. So that would be our recommendation so that we can strive. And I would notify the department today. I mean, it all depends what way to go here, what thoughts and what direction we get from the commission. If these dates are acceptable to you, we will move forward and notify the department of revenue. That concludes that report. A copy of my memo is attached to the agenda. And obviously it seems to me that this is the best way to go. The property, and I just got off the phone with property appraisal this morning. The property appraiser's office has sent out the notice of taxes, property taxes, and they have already started the collection process and they have started to distribute tax revenue to the city. I can go on record today to tell you, I don't know if you have had other calls. I checked with the office this morning to see if anyone has called to complain about the millage rate or the tax bill. And we have had zero calls. So the most important thing is, is that the five members of our governing body be present at the next meeting so that we can have a full commission. I don't know which way this is gonna go, but whatever way it goes, everybody gets an opportunity to weigh in on the recommendation of the manager or otherwise. The manager and the finance director, I mean, we've gone on record to say this. We would like for the commission to basically cement, if you would, the millage rate at 6.8858, but that is going to be discussed at that public hearing. But we have put it in writing. The letter from the Florida Department of Revenue has been attached in the packet and the notice adds that we have to comply with along with all the certification that goes with it has been included in the packet. That concludes my report. If you have any questions, I'm more than happy to take them.
